'''Jalen Brunson''' (born August 31, 1996) is an American basketball player who most recently played for the [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball]] where he completed his junior season for the [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|2017–18 team]] and declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]]. He completed his senior season for [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson High School]] in [[Lincolnshire, Illinois]] in the 2014–15 academic year.

According to [[ESPN]], he ended his junior year of high school as the number one point guard in the country and prior to his senior year he was rated number one by [[Scout.com]]. He was selected as the 2014 Illinois Boys Basketball [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards#Basketball|Gatorade Player of the Year]]. He was selected to participate in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] as well as the 2015 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and to represent the Team USA in the [[Nike Hoop Summit]]. As a senior, he repeated as the 2015 Illinois Gatorade Player of the Year and earned a third [[Associated Press]] All-state recognition (2nd first team). That year, he led Stevenson to the [[Illinois High School Association]] (IHSA) Class 4A championship. Following the season, he won [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]].

Brunson holds the IHSA playoff single-game and the IHSAt Class 4A championship game [[point (basketball)|scoring]] records and set the [[USA Basketball]] single-game [[assist (basketball)|assist]] record for the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. He [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|earned the MVP]] of the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] for the gold medal winning Team USA. He is the son of nine-year [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) veteran [[Rick Brunson]].

He began his college career as the [[2015–16 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2015–16 Big East Conference]] Preseason Freshman of the Year and was a Big East All-Freshman Team selection following the season. As a starter, he helped the [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|2015–16 Wildcats]] win the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship game]] of the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. As a sophomore, he was a unanimous [[2016–17 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2016–17 All-Big East first team]] selection for the [[2016–17 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|2016–17 Wildcats]]. As a junior, he was the [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|National Player of the Year]] and a Consensus first-team [[2018 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2018 All-Americans]] and he helped the [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|2017–18 Wildcats]] win the [[2018 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|championship game]] of the [[2018 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] to give Villanova their second National Championship in three years.

==Early life==
Born in [[New Brunswick, New Jersey]], Brunson was raised in southern New Jersey until sixth grade. He is the son of Rick and Sandra Brunson.<ref name=TVoJBl/> He has a sister Erica (born c. 2001).<ref name=JBUSAB>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/bios/brunson_jalen.html|title=Jalen Brunson|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]|accessdate=June 24, 2014|date=June 15, 2014}}</ref> His parents met at [[Temple University]] where Rick played for the [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Owls men's basketball]] team and Sandra played volleyball.<ref name=TVoJBl/> Rick went on to spend nine seasons in the NBA.<ref name=JBUSAB/> The family first settled in [[Cherry Hill, New Jersey]] but moved seven times before settling in [[Lincolnshire, Illinois]] in 2010 where Jalen played his high school career for [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson High School]].<ref name=TVoJBl>{{cite web|url=http://articles.philly.com/2014-06-21/sports/50741626_1_jalen-brunson-rick-brunson-temple-and-villanova|title=Temple, Villanova on Jalen Brunson's list|accessdate=June 24, 2014|date=June 21, 2014|publisher=[[Philly.com]]|author=Breen, Matt|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:20150401 MCDAAG Jalen Brunson.JPG|thumb|right]]
On May 5, 2014, [[USA Basketball]] announced the 21 athletes (including Brunson) invited to try out from June 10 to 19 for the 12-member USA national team for the June 20–24, [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/news-rumors/other-news/2014/05/usa-basketball-announces-u18-training-camp-roster/|title=USA Basketball Announces U18 Training Camp Roster|accessdate=May 16, 2014|date=May 5, 2014|work=[[SLAM Magazine]]}}</ref> Eventually, 24 players tried out for the team and the roster was cut to 15 on June 12.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_finalists.html|title=15 Finalists Selected For 2014 USA Men's U18 National Team|accessdate=June 13, 2014|date=June 12, 2014|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref>  Brunson made the final 12-man roster that was announced on June 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_team_.html|title=USA Men's U18 National Team Selected|accessdate=June 16, 2014|date=June 15, 2014|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref> In the opening game, Brunson surpassed [[Stephon Marbury]]'s 12 assists against Brazil in the 1994 FIBA Americas U18 Championship by recording 13 against Uruguay to set a new USA Basketball U18 single-game assist record.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_game_01.html|title=2014 USA Basketball Men's U18 National Team Races To Record-Setting 156-58 Opening Victory Over Uruguay|accessdate=June 24, 2014|date=June 20, 2014|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fibalivestats.com/matches/18/12/06/03/72a7RQ2yDPyuQ/|title=2014 Uruguay v. USA|accessdate=June 24, 2014|date=June 20, 2014|publisher=[[FIBA]]}}</ref> The United States claimed a gold medal in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_game_05.html|title=USA Basketball Men's U18 National Team Claims 2014 FIBA Americas U18 Championship Gold Medal With 113-79 Victory Over Canada|accessdate=June 25, 2014|date=June 24, 2014|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref> On August 16, 2014, Brunson was named to the Nike Global Challenge USA All-Tournament team along with [[Stephen Zimmerman]], [[D J Hogg]], [[Malik Monk]], [[Jaylen Brown]] and [[Edrice Adebayo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nikeinc.com/news/usa-west-defeats-usa-east-in-nike-global-championship-game#/inline/32678|title=USA West Defeats USA East in Nike Global Challenge Game|accessdate=August 19, 2014|date=August 18, 2014|publisher=[[Nike, Inc.]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/410699?referrer_id=806539|title=Nike Global All-Tournament Team: USA|accessdate=August 19, 2014|date=August 16, 2014|publisher=D1Circuit.com|author=Kinsky, Alec}}</ref> Brunson led the Midwest team to a third-place finish in the eight-team tournament.<ref name=SJBtpbIV/>

On June 18, 2015 Brunson was announced as a member of the 12-man 2015 USA Basketball Men’s U19 World Cup Team for the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/06/usa-mens-u19-team-named.aspx|title=USA Basketball 2015 Men’s U19 World Championship Team Named|accessdate=June 20, 2015|date=June 18, 2015|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref> Brunson earned [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|MVP of the tournament]], after leading the team with 5.6 assists and 2.1 steals for the tournament. He posted a game-high 30 points in the semifinals against Greece,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/07/usa-u19-men-defeat-greece.aspx|title=USA Men’s U19 Team Out-Battles Host Greece For 82-76 Win|accessdate=July 6, 2015|date=July 4, 2015|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref> and he tallied a team-high 14 points including 6 in overtime as well as 7 assists, 5 rebounds and a steal in the gold medal game against Croatia. Brunson tied teammate [[Harry Giles (basketball)|Harry Giles]], with a 14.0 average for the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/07/usa-u19-men-win-gold-medal.aspx|title=
USA Men Edge Croatia 79-71 In Overtime To Stake Claim On FIBA U19 World Championship Gold Medal|accessdate=July 6, 2015|date=July 5, 2015|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/news/usa-fight-off-valiant-effort-from-croatia-to-repeat-u19-title|title=USA fight off valiant effort from Croatia to repeat U19 title |accessdate=July 6, 2015|date=July 5, 2015|publisher=[[FIBA]]}}</ref> He dominated in the final two games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2015/7/6/8900453/jalen-brunson-villanova-usa-basketball-u19-tournament-mvp|title=Jalen Brunson is going to be a problem at Villanova|accessdate=November 12, 2015|date=July 6, 2015|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|author=O'Donnell, Ricky}}</ref> Based on this performance, he was recognized as the [[USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year]], on December 21, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/news-events/news/2015/12/2015-male-athlete-of-the-year.aspx|title=Jalen Brunson Named 2015 USA Basketball Male Athlete Of The Year|accessdate=April 6, 2016|date=December 21, 2015|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref>
